Intertextile Shenzhen Apparel Fabrics 2026 will debut its Future Horizons Forum and Innovation Studio from June 9-11 at the Shenzhen Convention & Exhibition Center.
With partners including PolyU, THEi, Wuyi University and AIHF, the fair will spotlight textile innovation, AI, sustainability, hemp materials and advanced fabrics from exhibitors across 11 countries and regions.

title: Textile CEOs shift 2026 priorities beyond growth targets
summary:
Textile CEOs are shifting priorities in 2026 as growth gives way to resilience amid volatile energy costs, stricter sustainability rules, supply-chain risks and AI-driven changes.
Manufacturers are focusing on energy efficiency, compliance, traceability and smarter operations.
Industry leadership is increasingly being defined by adaptability and risk management rather than scale and cost alone.

title: Nylon chain cracks: Margin squeeze pulls DTY & CPL prices down
summary:
Nylon buyers face a tighter Q3 cost base as crude-linked caprolactam inflation keeps DTY yarn about 17–19 per cent above February levels, despite weak downstream demand.
Mills are buying only against confirmed orders, limiting further spikes but not reversing cost pressure.
Brands may need to renegotiate, absorb margins or lock supply before another crude breakout.

title: India launches Bharat Tex 2026 app with AI-powered assistance tool
summary:
India has launched the Bharat Tex 2026 app to enhance the experience of buyers, delegates, speakers, sourcing consultants, partners, exhibitors and visitors at the country’s largest global textile event, scheduled to be held from July 14 to 17 in New Delhi. 
The app can be used by participants to access event information, find exhibitors, schedule meetings, navigate the venue and receive real-time updates.

title: ICE cotton sees mixed trend as rain forecasts weaken sentiment
summary:
ICE cotton futures remained under pressure as improving rainfall forecasts across major US cotton-growing regions eased crop concerns and weighed on market sentiment.
The July 2026 contract fell 0.89 per cent to 81.60 cents, marking its fifth decline in seven sessions.
Lower crude oil prices, subdued trading activity, and weak speculative participation also added bearish pressure on cotton prices.

title: Tariffs did not rewire apparel sourcing. They exposed its limits.
summary:
US apparel sourcing is shifting away from China, but TexPro data shows diversification remains Asia-led, not nearshoring-led.
Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia and Indonesia are gaining relevance, while Mexico and CAFTA-DR remain limited.
The real 2026 advantage is qualified optionality: audited, scalable, compliant suppliers that can absorb tariff, legal and supply shocks.

title: China, US to discuss tariff reduction framework on $30 bn trade
summary:
China and the US have agreed in principle to discuss a reciprocal tariff reduction framework covering products worth $30 billion or more on each side. 
The identified goods may receive most-favoured-nation or lower tariff rates, signalling a possible easing of tariff tensions and a structured push to stabilise bilateral trade and support wider global open cooperation.

title: Retail’s new shipping reality: Reroutes, DDP & constant volatility
summary:
DDP is becoming critical for cross-border retail as stricter customs, DPP and EPR requirements increase shipment complexity. 
By charging duties and taxes upfront, brands can reduce abandonment and improve customer transparency. 
Rising rerouting activity shows global shipping volatility is now a structural challenge, not a temporary disruption.

title: Higher oil costs, El Nino to shrink FY27 Indian growth to 6.7%: Ind-Ra
summary:
Ind-Ra has projected India’s GDP growth at 6.7 per cent YoY in FY27. 
The agency believes higher fuel and food prices due to the Middle East conflict’s uncertainty and the likely impact of evolving El Nino on agriculture from mid-2026 will pull down growth in FY27. 
A $10/bbl rise in crude oil prices could reduce GDP growth by 44 bps, while a 10-per cent reduction in capex could lower growth to 6 per cent.

title: Morocco, Bangladesh to deepen cooperation in trade & investment
summary:
Morocco and Bangladesh recently agreed to deepen cooperation in trade, investment, agriculture, skill development and multilateral affairs when the latter’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam met the former’s Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita in Rabat. 
Islam reiterated Bangladesh's interest in promoting eco-friendly jute and jute goods in the Moroccan market.

title: US President Trump extends AGOA till 2026 end
summary:
Exporters in many African nations have regained duty-free access to the US after the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) was extended till 2026 end by a US presidential proclamation. 
The extension follows a lapse in the programme in late 2025, which had caused uncertainty for African exporters dependent on US market access. 
Gabon was reinstated as an AGOA beneficiary, reversing its 2023 removal.

title: US' VF Corporation returns to FY26 growth, Q4 revenue up
summary:
VF Corporation has returned to growth in FY26, with revenue up 1 per cent and ex-Dickies revenue rising 4 per cent. 
Margins expanded, operating income reached $577 million, and leverage improved to 3.1x. 
Q4 revenue rose 1 per cent, led by Americas momentum, The North Face and Timberland growth, while VF reinstated FY27 guidance for continued growth and higher margins.

title: Tiruppur’s synthetic bet meets the oil wall
summary:
Tiruppur’s MMF and performancewear pivot remains strategically necessary, but 2026 cost shocks are testing its economics.
TexPro data shows knitted exports down 8.6 per cent in January-February 2026, while crude-linked polyester, dyeing, LPG and packaging costs have surged.
The cluster’s next advantage will depend on scale, backward linkages, contracts and cost pass-through discipline.

title: Georgia’s apparel imports expand as post-war spending strengthens
summary:
Georgia’s apparel imports rose 16.5 per cent year on year to $97.15 million in Q1 2026, supported by stronger domestic consumption and higher clothing spending after the Russia-Ukraine war reshaped migration and economic patterns.
Trousers, T-shirts, and jerseys led imports, while the country’s apparel market continued its strong post-2021 expansion trend.

title: Bangladesh garment sector distant from renewable energy target: Study
summary:
Bangladesh garment units are quite far from meeting clean energy consumption targets due to high renewable energy costs, limited rooftop space, and policy bottlenecks that are slowing adoption across the sector, a study revealed. 
Eighty-eight per cent of respondents cited high installation costs as a barrier to renewable energy adoption, while 42 per cent pointed to high maintenance costs.

title: Finland’s Amer Sports raises 2026 guidance after strong Q1 growth
summary:
Amer Sports raised its 2026 revenue, margin and EPS guidance after Q1 revenue grew 32 per cent to $1.945 billion, driven by strong double-digit growth across all regions. 
Technical Apparel rose 33 per cent, Outdoor Performance 42 per cent, and Ball & Racquet Sports 13 per cent. 
The operating profit increased 50 per cent, while adjusted EPS rose 47 per cent to $0.38.

title: Wide legs, dark washes, Y2K cuts: Inside denim’s Trends of 2026
summary:
Denim demand is rising as consumers move beyond skinny jeans towards Y2K-inspired, relaxed and tailored silhouettes. 
Gen Z is driving the shift through thrift, vintage appeal, influencer-led styling and sustainability values. 
Coloured denim, dark indigo washes, low-rise fits and experimental cuts are gaining momentum across fashion markets.

title: Cambodia’s apparel exports rise 9.6% in January-April 2026
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports rose 9.61 per cent to $3.45 billion in January–April 2026, accounting for 31.1 per cent of total exports and reaffirming the sector’s importance to the economy.
Strong April growth and gains across knitted and woven apparel reflected resilient sourcing demand, while rising cotton imports signalled changing raw-material preferences among manufacturers.

title: US’ Aramark’s Q2 revenue grows on US, international gains
summary:
Aramark has reported revenue of $4.9 billion in Q2 FY26, up 15 per cent YoY, driven by new business wins and growth across US and international operations. 
Operating income rose 26 per cent to $220 million, while adjusted EPS grew 40 per cent. 
Cash flow strengthened, client retention exceeded 98 per cent, and the company raised its organic revenue outlook.

title: Why Spring/Summer 2026 fashion colours reflect global chaos
summary:
Spring/Summer 2026 fashion is balancing bold and neutral palettes, with tomato red emerging as the standout colour alongside shades such as lost lilac, moody blue, soured citrus and jaded teal.  
Industry experts say earthy neutrals are becoming wardrobe foundations, while brighter tones are increasingly used as accents to add energy, nostalgia and emotional appeal.
